derivation: from (to swell (with young), i.e. bend, curve);

occurrences.text: And, behold, there arose a great tempest in the sea, insomuch that the ship was covered with the waves: but he was asleep.
But the ship was now in the midst of the sea, tossed with waves: for the wind was contrary.
And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full.
Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
